headline: H.R. 195 would have funded federal agencies through February 8, 2018, ended a government shutdown, extended children's health insurance, and delayed several health-related taxes, but the Senate did not take it up.
what_it_does: This bill would have combined four separate parts. Division A would have limited free printed copies of the Federal Register sent to Members of Congress and federal offices unless they requested them. Division B would have extended temporary federal spending authority through February 8, 2018, ended a government shutdown, and added funding flexibility for several agencies, along with pay for furloughed workers. Division C would have extended the Children's Health Insurance Program and related Medicaid and CHIP options through FY2023. Division D would have delayed the medical device excise tax moratorium, the Cadillac tax, and the health insurer fee for certain years.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees furloughed during the lapse in appropriations
who_it_affects.how: They would have been compensated for pay lost during the shutdown that began around January 20, 2018.

who_it_affects.group: Children enrolled in or eligible for CHIP and Medicaid
who_it_affects.how: Their state coverage programs would have had federal funding extended through FY2023.
They would have avoided the 2.3% excise tax on medical device sales in 2018 and 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Employers offering high-cost employer-sponsored health coverage
who_it_affects.how: The Cadillac tax would have taken effect in 2022 instead of 2020.
They would not have owed the annual market-share-based fee for 2019.
Demonstration projects providing summer meals would have received funding flexibility to be operational by May 2018.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses seeking general business loans
who_it_affects.how: The Small Business Administration would have gained funding flexibility to meet higher demand for section 7(a) loans.

who_it_affects.group: Public housing agencies in areas with 2017 or 2018 presidential disaster declarations
who_it_affects.how: They would have received adjustments to Section 8 housing voucher renewal funding and administrative fee rules.
